text:
Sam: Quick sync — Orchid Systems wants their POC Private deployment wired up today. They requested VPC peering (control plane in our account) + a small on-prem NAT for egress. Can infra confirm the minimal route requirements?

Maya: @Sam I sketched what we usually ask for. Short checklist: 1) Customer CIDR(s) 2) Desired cross-account peering type (peer vs AWS PrivateLink) 3) Subnet CIDR for the Private control plane ENIs 4) Route tables that send model traffic to our peering VPN. Do we have their CIDRs?

Sam: I have their CIDRs in the SOW: 10.40.0.0/16 (apps), 10.41.128.0/18 (onprem). They prefer peering over PrivateLink for this POC.

Ravi: OK. For peering with hosted control plane we need them to add a route in their route table: destination = 10.200.0.0/16 -> peering-conn-id. On our side the route is destination = 10.40.0.0/16 -> peering-conn-id. Also confirm we don't overlap any subnets.

Maya: Also watch for 0.0.0.0/0 propagation — they must NOT propagate a default route into the peered RTBs. If they plan to use a NAT for egress, provide the NAT gateway IPs so we can whitelist outbound flows from our control plane.

Nora: Security note: we need an allowlist for the management plane: TCP 443 from their control-plane subnets to our control plane ENIs. Provide the exact ENI IPs or we can open to the peering CIDR with justification. Also include the cert fingerprint for mutual TLS validation in the security questionnaire.

Lee: For the POC keying: we will issue a temporary API credential scoped to the POC account. That credential will be bound to the peered network and expire in 14 days. Client asked about private DNS — we can support conditional forwarding but they'll need to create a Route53 inbound resolver rule pointing to our IPs.

Sam: Can someone drop the exact example route commands I can paste to their cloud engineer?

Ravi: Sure, example AWS CLI for their side:```bash
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0abcd1234 --destination-cidr-block 10.200.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0a1b2c3d
```And on our side:```bash
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0ffff2222 --destination-cidr-block 10.40.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0a1b2c3d
```Replace IDs with real ones. Also confirm both sides accept the peering and enable DNS resolution (`modify-vpc-peering-connection-options --requester-region us-west-2 --allow-vpc-dns-resolution`).

Maya: For subnets: we recommend dedicating 2 /24s for the control plane ENIs and 1 /24 for model egress NAT. Keep security groups tight: only our control-plane port and SSH if needed for troubleshooting (temporary).

Nora: Add this to the security questionnaire answer: "We require VPC peering with strict route entries and hosts limited to the peered CIDRs. TLS 1.2+ enforced, mutual auth optional for POC but recommended for production."

Sam: I'll send this to Orchid's cloud team. If they push PrivateLink instead, any blockers?

Ravi: PrivateLink is fine but requires them to create an interface endpoint in each AZ and accept our service endpoint. DNS and SGs are different: we give them service name and ENIs are in their account. Slightly more setup but avoids cross-account route changes. For a quick POC peering is usually faster.

deploy-bot: Deployment note: peering confirmed pending acceptance by requester (Orchid). CI/CD will pause automated rollout until peering is active.

Sam: Thanks all. I'll ping once they accept and paste their endpoint IPs. :thumbsup:

Maya: If they need a sample CloudFormation snippet for the route and endpoint, say the word and I'll drop it in the ticket.

Sam: Please do.
